title: Multiprotocol Conformance Smokebench — structured outputs & toolcall regression bridge
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a compact, automated smokebench that validates API compatibility across streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured output layers. The aim is to provide a fast, repeatable CI gate that exercises realistic golden prompts, checks message boundary semantics for multiplexed streaming, validates JSON/NDJSON schema fallbacks, asserts toolcall idempotency, and catches regressions introduced by kernel scheduling or KV cache priming. This ticket covers test design, harness implementation, CI integration, and initial stabilization of flaky cases.
acceptance_criteria: Smokebench runs in under 7 minutes in the CI job and returns exit code 0 on expected pass cases
At least 12 golden prompts exercised covering: partial-chunk scenarios, interleaved toolcalls, structured-output schema fallback, and streaming backpressure simulation
CI job (compat/multiprotocol-smokebench) is added to PR gates for runtime and endpoint-shim repos
Failure modes produce human-readable diagnostics: seed, captured chunks, reconstructed JSON payload, and PR suggestion template
Observed flakiness rate in 50 consecutive runs <= 3%; flaky cases triaged into follow-up tickets with reproducible seeds
proposed_tests: Partial-chunk injection harness to assert JSON recovery and schema fallback
Toolcall idempotency scenarios with synthetic retries and exact-once expectations
KV cache priming sequence tests to detect sequence-number regressions
Backpressure emulator to validate chunking boundaries and continuity tokens
Cross-variant compatibility matrix (quantized vs full-precision model variants)
comments: 2026-02-11 — Aisha Raman: Kickoff notes added. Scope limited to a fast smokebench (not full golden-suite) so we can get a PR-gate in 2 sprints.
2026-02-18 — Miguel Ortega: PoC harness committed to compat-tests repo. Uses deterministic seeds and an NDJSON roundtrip validator. Initial run completes in ~9m; need to shave 2m for CI budget.
2026-02-22 — Shweta Kapoor (PM): Prioritize partial-chunk scenarios and toolcall idempotency; suggested dropping some slow KV cache variants from initial run.
2026-02-25 — Eng review (runtime team): Kernel scheduling can add 200-400ms variance; added warmup/priming step to reduce cold-start noise.
2026-03-01 — Design review (Danielle Wu): Structured-output fallback cases need explicit schema assertion and suggest including a compact schema coverage table in diagnostics.
2026-03-05 — Miguel Ortega: CI job optimized — moved 2 long examples to nightly; smokebench now completes in 6m35s on our CI runners.
2026-03-09 — Flakiness analysis: 3/200 runs showed partial-chunk reorder due to interleaving; created ENG-40722 to harden chunk serializer and ENG-40723 for additional logging.
2026-03-12 — Merge: harness impl PR #518 merged; CI job added to runtime PR gating but flagged as opt-in for 48h to monitor false positives.
decisions: Smokebench will be small (<=12 prompts) and focused on high-risk compatibility vectors rather than exhaustive coverage
Deterministic seeds + captured chunk replay will be stored with failures for triage (gs:// storage), not in CI logs
Initial gating is opt-in to reduce noise; move to required gate after 2 weeks of stable runs
Use NDJSON roundtrip validator as the canonical structured-output assertion to match downstream consumers
monitoring: Alert: job failure rate > 1% over 24h triggers on-call notification to infra-team
test_data_examples: golden: 'reorder-toolcall-interleaving-v1' — expects toolcall sequence preserved and JSON payloads reconstructed
golden: 'partial-json-incremental-v1' — expects NDJSON fallback when final chunk is malformed
golden: 'kv-priming-seq-3' — verifies KV cache continuity across warmup and main request
golden: 'backpressure-chunk-skip' — emulator injects slow consumer; assert continuity tokens are present
